**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] User has been doing model building for about 3 months.
- [FACT] User started with a 1/48 scale F-16C Fighting Falcon.
- [FACT] User is currently working on a 1/35 scale T-34 tank.
- [FACT] User is also working on a 1/24 scale Ford Mustang GT500.
- [PREFERENCE] User is looking for tips on achieving a realistic rust effect on their model tank.
- [PREFERENCE] User has tried using oil washes but is not satisfied with the results.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To achieve a realistic rust effect, the assistant suggested understanding rust, using a good primer and base coat, and mixing a range of rust colors from orange to brown to red.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended using texture mediums like Vallejo's Texture paste or Mig Productions' Rust Texture to add depth and dimension to the rust effect.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised building up the rust effect in layers, creating streaks and running effects, and using drybrushing and weathering powders for added realism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of recommended products, including Vallejo Model Color rust paints, Mig Productions rust paints, AK Interactive rust paints, and Tamiya weathering masters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that Mig Productions' rust paints have a unique formula that mimics real rust and offers a realistic color range.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant highlighted that Mig Productions' rust paints are easy to blend and can create a range of textures.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for using Mig Productions' rust paints, including starting with a light coat and mixing with Vallejo Model Color paints.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that common mistakes beginners make in weathering and rust effects include over-weathering, inconsistent weathering, incorrect rust colors, and not referencing real-world examples.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasized the importance of a good base coat and blending weathering effects for a natural look.
